content: Currently, all API on torsors in Mathlib is written exclusively in additive form, because it is mainly used for affine vector spaces. I've opened #38896 last week changing that because I need multiplicative torsors for G-principal bundles, but it has sat without a review so far - do we have anyone who knows these algebraic hierarchy files well willing to change that? :)
cc @Eric Wieser who submitted a similar PR #8608 years ago already, which unfortunately never got merged. But really, if anyone else could take a look that would also be great

I've also opened a second PR #39130 on multiplicative topological torsors now. What's still missing for both changes is file renames (e.g. Algebra.AddTorsor.Basic to Algebra.Torsor.Basic), because I haven't worked with module deprecations before - am I understanding it right that the process for that is to move the files first, and then add module deprecations in a follow-up PR?
Yes: first just the file move, then the module deprecation.

Bumping this since it has been another week without a review - #38896 on multiplicative torsors is still ready for / waiting for review, complete with the file moves and a follow-up PR adding module deprecations. The diff is somewhat large because of the file move and the number of lemmas affected, but I would hope that since the PR mostly only multiplicativises existing declarations it still shouldn't take too much effort to review.
It might speed up review to split the PR into a file move and the multiplicativisation. I can certainly review the first one quickly.

I see, thanks - I've removed the file rename from #38896 again now. I'll create a separate PR for the file rename once #38896 and maybe also the PR on multiplicative topological torsors have been merged (since if we're going with one separate PR for the rename and one separate PR for the module deprecations, I suppose it is better to wait until the PR for topological torsors is merged too so we don't have do the same again then).

Bumping this again - the PR is now a month old, still waiting for a first review and still blocking me from PRing more things on torsors since I would rather not have too many dependent PRs open at the same time

I am not an official reviewer but I took a look and it looks good to me
I wonder if you merge the latest master, it will trigger the new declaration diff script, so we can quickly review and ensure there is no accidental drop of theorems

That is indeed a good suggestion, thanks - I wasn't aware of this new script. That should make reviewing a bit easier. In fact, as it turns out there actually even was an issue that the script pointed out - I didn't drop a theorem, but one of the lemma names generated by to_additive was different from the original additive name. I've pushed the fix for that, so hopefully the PR should now be good in that regard.

The first PR on multiplicative torsors is merged now - thanks! I've merged master on #39130 on topological torsors now (and fixed another wrong to_additive declaration name pointed out by the new diff script), so that should now be ready to review next

The PR renaming the involved files from AddTorsor to Torsor was merged four days ago already, but the follow-up PR #39134 adding module deprecations for the moved files was not - I imagine it would be good to get that merged soon too

though I guess now that mathlib 4.31.0 was released in the meantime already the inconvenience of having a release removing files without module deprecations is already there :man_facepalming: I didn't know another release was planned so soon
The usual schedule is a new release every 15+eps-th of the month
